note: Differences between the compatibility projection and an expected file that are accepted, by run and step. 'expected' is the value in the expected file and 'got' is what load -> derive_deps -> projection gives. The ids are those of EXCEPTIONS.md in the GRADE expectations work, continued (E17 and E18 are new, from the gate-2 follow-up); 'causes' holds the reason and the count of each id, and a class 'c' cause is a behaviour of GRADE or a defect of an expected file that agentpile deliberately does not copy. A difference not listed here fails the test; a listed one that does not occur also fails. SWE-agent and the other baselines (who_and_when, tau_bench, tau2_bench frozen, swe_gym_openhands, swe_rebench_openhands) have no difference, so they have no entry. The E3 entry compares against GRADE HEAD fe6e54d, not against the frozen baseline.

exceptions.reason: GRADE HEAD credits every result of a multi-call assistant message to the last call of that message (last_tc); the frozen rule pairs each result with its own call, by position because the data has no result ids. Message 51 issues three parallel calls; the customer record that carries L1002 is the first call's result (step 35), and HEAD attaches the later lookup to step 37, a call that returned an error.

E3.reason: GRADE HEAD credits every result of a multi-call assistant message to the last call of that message; the frozen rule pairs each result with its own call (EXCEPTIONS.md E3).

E17.reason: The last record of a run file is the page after the last action: it holds no action and no agent reply. GRADE's to_steps turns every record into a decision step and a tool step (the action type is 'noop' for an empty action), so the run gets two steps agentpile has no event for; the noop step also carries one edge when the final page was visited before. The reader keeps this record as the result of the last call, and a step for it would be an agent decision nobody took, which load() does not invent. Each affected run lists the step count (n_steps) and the two steps (tail) that only the expected file has.
